chunks: As for after the passing of the companions of his father,

for a period of time, his news and reports were reaching [the Shia] through the emissaries between him and his Shia, whose words were trusted and to whom reference was made regarding their religion and trustworthiness, and for the specific qualities they possessed of piety and integrity.
And perhaps we have mentioned a portion of their narratives in what follows.

key_terms.أَصْحَابِ أَبِيهِ: companions of his father (referring to the companions of Imam al-Hasan al-Askari)
key_terms.السُّفَرَاءِ: emissaries/ambassadors (the four prominent deputies of the Imam)

ai.seo_question: How did the Shia communicate with the Imam during the period of his occultation?
ai.summary: This passage highlights the institutionalized trust (thiqa) in the four emissaries (al-Sufara' al-Arba'a) during the Minor Occultation, emphasizing their role as reliable intermediaries who preserved religious authority and communal unity. Tusi underscores that their veracity and piety were well-established, providing the Shia community with a stable foundation for deriving religious rulings and maintaining spiritual connection with the Imam before the transition to the Major Occultation.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: After the companions of his father, communication was intact with him through the emissaries between him and his Shia, whose words were trusted and whose piety and trustworthiness made them reliable.
We may bring some of their narratives in this regard in the future.
